shape_notes: Conventions observed in the 181 already-filled records (e.g. herb.ma_huang, herb.gui_zhi, herb.zi_su_ye, herb.sheng_jiang, herb.xiang_ru): (1) actions_en is a 1:1, same-order translation of functions_zh — one English action phrase per zh entry, Bensky/Wiseman-style verb phrases with capitalized TCM entities (Lung, Cold, Qi, Yang, Ying/Wei, Middle, Dampness, Summerheat); verb person is mixed in existing data (both "Induces sweating..." and "Release the muscle layer..."), proposals here use third-person -s consistently. Compound zh entries (containing 、 or ，) stay a single en string with sub-actions joined by "; " (matches "Warm and unblock the channels; disperse Cold and relieve pain"). (2) condition_tags_en is a 1:1, same-order translation of condition_tags_zh — short pattern/disease noun tags ("Wind-cold excess exterior", "Cold-congealing dysmenorrhea"), NOT derived from indications_zh. Finding: every one of the 190 records with empty condition_tags_en also has empty condition_tags_zh (verified programmatically), so per the no-extraction rule there are zero condition_tags_en proposals — that gap cannot be closed by translation alone.
